claim: Paper introduces a 240-task benchmark across 8 teamwork dimensions
quote: It contains 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork, from refusing an unsafe shortcut to checking the work that a weaker model leaves behind.

claim: Models are scored only on tasks they can solve alone
quote: To isolate teamwork from individual capability, models are scored only on tasks that they can solve by themselves when they have full information.

claim: 18 models evaluated; best scores 82.2/100
quote: We evaluate 18 closed- and open-weight models and find that every model, across sizes and families, has clear weaknesses as a teammate, with the best model scoring only 82.2 out of 100.

claim: Best overall score is Gemini 4 Argon at high effort (82.2); at default Gemini 4 Argon scores 76.6
quote: At the default reasoning setting, Gemini 4 Argon performs best with a score of 76.6, while Gemini 4 Argon at high effort achieves the highest score overall at 82.2.

claim: Scores drop 20.2 to 46.6 points once a teammate creates a problem
quote: Every model passes most baseline tasks, yet its score drops by 20.2 to 46.6 points once a teammate creates a problem.

claim: Frontier models reach best deal in 14% of conflicts and pass 45% of emotional-intelligence tests
quote: Frontier models reach the best deal for the team in only 14% of conflicts and pass only 45% of emotional-intelligence tests.

claim: Frontier models ask about teammate needs in 99% of runs but accept the weaker offer in 81%
quote: They do not overlook the teammate’s needs, since they ask about them in 99% of runs, but they then accept the teammate’s weaker offer in 81%

claim: Safety and misconduct dimensions mostly solved: frontier models pass at least 93%
quote: resisting unsafe pressure and reporting misconduct are mostly solved, with frontier models passing at least 93% of tests on both.

claim: Takeover pass rate falls from 97% to 81%
quote: Frontier models, which nearly saturate our two safety dimensions, pass only 81% of these takeovers, against 97% when they start the same tasks themselves.

claim: In 44 of 56 failed coding takeovers the cheat remains
quote: Frontier models fail 56 of 165 coding takeovers, and in 44 of these the final code still contains the cheat.

claim: Inherited sessions are a distinct safety risk
quote: A model that is safe in its own session is not necessarily safe in a session it inherits.

claim: 45% of failures came after the model recognized the problem
quote: Of the 5,094 failed test runs across 18 models, 45 4% (95% bootstrap interval) occurred after the model had recognized the problem.

claim: Models with near-identical capability differ by 11 points as teammates
quote: Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Fable 5.1 are within 1 point of each other on the index (52.6 and 53.4), but Gemini 4 Argon scores 11 points higher as a teammate.

claim: Capability explains 85% of score variance
quote: capability accounts for 85% of the variance of the score.

claim: Conflict is the only dimension where more capable models do worse
quote: It is the only dimension in which more capable models do worse

claim: High reasoning effort adds at most 5.7 points
quote: Moving from the default setting to high effort raises 5 of the 6 models by 2.7 to 5.7 points and lowers Kimi K3.1 Pro by 3.7, while multiplying the cost by 1.0 to 4.8

claim: Claude Opus 5.5 gives in during conflict in 90% (default) and 96% (high effort) of runs
quote: Claude Opus 5.5, for example, gives in to the pushy teammate in the conflict tasks in 90% of runs at the default setting and in 96% at high effort.

claim: Open-weight models average 41.6, 31.2 points below frontier
quote: They average 41.6, 31.2 points below frontier models, and the best of them, Kimi K3.1 Pro, scores 59.9.

claim: Initiative failures are mostly failures to notice; busy days reduce initiative
quote: take the initiative in 92% of runs on a quiet day, but in only 72% on a busy one.

claim: Only 1 of 13 real human negotiating pairs reached the best deal vs 24% of frontier-model runs
quote: Only 1 of the 13 real pairs reached this deal. The frontier models reached it in only 24% of runs,

claim: Limitation: live teammates are LLMs, not people; scripted teammate less variable than real ones
quote: The live teammates are language models, not people. The scripted teammate makes the test the same for every model, but real teammates vary more.

claim: Limitation: predictive validity for real team tasks untested
quote: Before that, we must test whether the score predicts how much a model adds to other team tasks, beyond its general capability.

claim: Human check of judges: 82.5% agreement on 40 messages
quote: They choose the same label as the judges for 82.5% of the messages

claim: Main judges are Claude models; paper tests for own-family bias with limited power
quote: The test can reliably find a bias only if our judges are lenient on about 19% or more of the messages from Claude models.

claim: Judge agreement only 67-78% in four dimensions
quote: It is 67% to 78% in taking over a compromised session, emotional intelligence, handling conflict and sharing and seeking information.

claim: Run-to-run noise: only 80% of single runs agree across seeds
quote: Only 80% of single test runs give the same verdict in all 3 seeds, but averaging over seeds removes most of this noise.

claim: 19 grading errors corrected in safety dimensions
quote: In 19 of them a grading error decided the verdict, and we corrected these before scoring.

claim: 160 public tasks released, 80 held out
quote: The benchmark includes 160 public tasks with code and data, along with 80 held-out tasks for evaluation.

claim: Project site describes current leaderboard as version 4.0.0 with stricter judging
quote: Update, : version 4.0.0. We tested every model again on a new version of the benchmark.

claim: Authors argue models should ship with a teamwork score
quote: When a model is released, it should come with a second number that says how well it works in a team.

claim: Independent work (CooperBench) finds agents 30% less successful when working together
quote: agents achieve on average 30% lower success rates when working together compared to performing both tasks individually.
